turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I’m only sitting here because my wife and everybody else keeps acting like I’m just making it all up, like I’m imagining the whole thing. But I’m not blind, and I’m not stupid. I know exactly what’s going on. It’s her relative, see? He’s been coming into this house—my house—just to get at me. 

I work at the fabrication plant, right? I put things together for a living. I know exactly where things belong down to the millimeter. So when I go into my garage, my tools... they don't just move themselves. I have a very specific system. I'll leave my 3/8-inch drive right on the pegboard, and suddenly I come home and it's sitting over on the band saw. Who does that? And it’s not just the shop, either. Every single weekend, I make my plans to head down to the lake, get out on the water, do a little fishing and get some peace... and every single time, without fail, the plans get spoiled. It’s not by accident! The truck battery is suddenly drained, or my tackle box is completely reorganized backwards, or the lock on the gate is jammed up. Every weekend! 

It's exhausting, having to watch your back in your own property. And after all these months of dealing with this, keeping track of every little thing he messes with... I mean, I can see it plain as day now. He’s been trying to take over my place. He wants to push me out of my own home, take what's mine, and nobody wants to listen to me about it. They just send me to a doctor instead.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that his wife's relative is secretly entering his home, moving his tools, and sabotaging his plans in an effort to push him out, maintaining this belief despite his family telling him he is imagining it.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard any voices or seen things that other people couldn't see or hear?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? Seeing things? No, no, no. See, that’s... that's exactly what my wife is trying to tell everybody, that I’m sitting around hearing ghosts or seeing things floating in the air. I don't hear voices. I hear the air compressor kicking on in the shop, I hear the dog barking next door, I hear normal, everyday things. I’m not crazy. I’m not sitting in the dark talking to myself or seeing shadows in the corners. 

What I'm talking about is physical, tangible evidence. You can't hallucinate a drained truck battery! You can't hallucinate a wrench moving from a pegboard to a band saw. I mean, think about it, if I was seeing things or hearing voices, don't you think I'd be messing up at the plant? At work, if I'm off by a fraction of a millimeter, a whole assembly stops. I have to have perfect vision, perfect focus. I don't have time to be seeing things that aren't there. I see what is exactly in front of my face. 

And what's in front of my face is that someone is coming onto my property, touching my things, putting their hands on my equipment. It's not a voice in my head that jams up a gate lock, okay? It takes a physical person with a physical tool, maybe a piece of wire or some grit, to jam a lock up like that. So no, I don't hear any voices. I just see the mess he leaves behind, and I seem to be the only one around here who actually opens my eyes and looks at it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a firm, fixed belief that someone is secretly coming onto his property and tampering with his equipment, strongly implying a persecutory delusion.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly and repeatedly denies hearing voices or seeing things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: Have you generally had trouble trusting other people throughout your life, or did this kind of suspicion only start with this relative?
turns.patient_response:
Trouble trusting people? No, doc, you've got the completely wrong idea about me. I'm not some... some paranoid hermit hiding in a bunker, looking out the blinds at everybody who walks by. Throughout my life? I've been a team player my whole life. 

I mean, look at my job. At the fabrication plant, you have to trust the guys on the line with you. It's a precision operation. If I'm doing the final assembly on a custom housing unit, I have to trust that Jimmy down in stamping did his job right, and that the welders didn't leave any slag. I've worked with Jimmy for fifteen years. I trust him completely. I'd give him the shirt off my back, and he'd do the same for me. You can't do what I do for a living if you're constantly second-guessing the guy standing next to you. And in my neighborhood? I've always been a "handshake is a contract" kind of guy. You ask anybody I grew up with, anybody I used to play cards with... well, I haven't had time for cards much lately because I have to guard my shop, but if you asked them, they'd tell you. I'm a straight shooter. I take people at their word. 

So no, I don't have some lifelong problem with trusting people. This whole thing... it only started with him because he's the one doing it! Before he started coming around, before my wife decided she needed to invite him over for every little holiday and Sunday dinner, everything in my life was fine. My tools stayed exactly where I put them. My truck started on the first turn of the key. 

And you call it suspicion, but that's the wrong word. Suspicion means you're guessing. It means you're not sure. I'm not guessing here. It's not a "suspicion" if you have the proof right there in front of you, plain as day. You see what I mean? It's like... if a guy walks up and punches you in the arm, you don't have "trust issues" with him, you have a bruise! And I'm looking at the bruises on my property every single day. He leaves his fingerprints on my life every weekend. So no, I trust people just fine. I just don't trust *him*, because I'd have to be an absolute idiot to trust a guy who is actively trying to run me off my own land.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient exhibits a fixed, persecutory belief that a relative is sabotaging his property and trying to run him off his land, insisting it is absolute fact rather than a suspicion.

turns.doctor_question: Have you recently experienced any major medical problems, head injuries, or physical health changes?
turns.patient_response:
Medical problems? Head injuries? No, no, I'm healthy as a horse. I mean, look at me. You don't work the line at the fabrication plant for thirty years if you're falling apart. It's physical work, you know? You're on your feet all day, lifting, bending, torqueing down bolts... it takes a toll, sure, maybe a little stiffness in the lower back when it rains, but that's just life. That's just getting older. 

I haven't been to a hospital since... well, I had my appendix out when I was nineteen, but that's ancient history. Never hit my head, never been knocked out, never even had a concussion playing football back in high school. My blood pressure is fine, my heart is ticking along just perfectly. I eat right—well, mostly right, my wife makes sure I get my vegetables, even if I'd rather just have a steak—and I don't drink like some of the guys at the plant who are closing down the bar every Friday night. I'll have a beer while I'm working in the shop, but that's it. 

So, no, there's absolutely nothing wrong with my brain, and there's nothing wrong with my body. I'm completely sharp. I have to be sharp for my job, like I told you. If my head wasn't screwed on straight, if I was having some kind of... of medical episode or a stroke or something, I wouldn't be able to read the blueprints. I wouldn't be able to calibrate the machinery. I'd be making mistakes left and right, and my foreman would have me out the door before lunchtime. 

But I'm not making mistakes. I'm doing my job perfectly. The only problem I have is this guy coming into my house and messing with my stuff. And it's honestly insulting that everyone keeps trying to find some kind of... of medical excuse for what's happening. "Oh, maybe he hit his head, maybe he's sick, maybe he's just confused." I'm not confused! I'm perfectly healthy, and I'm perfectly aware of what's going on around me. If anything, the stress of having to deal with this relative is going to give me a heart attack eventually, but right now? Physically? I'm absolutely fine.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient insists that someone is coming into his house and messing with his belongings, maintaining this belief despite others telling him he is just confused or sick.
symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly states that he is not making mistakes and is doing his job perfectly.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient denies being confused and asserts that his mind is completely sharp.
